question: In real small-claims courts, did a baby-faced defendant always do better than a mature-faced one?
answer: No: it depended on the charge. Leslie Zebrowitz and Susan McDonald found baby-faced defendants more likely to win cases alleging intentional harm, and less likely to win cases alleging negligence. A face that looks innocent also looks naive and careless. The same round cheeks helped against one accusation and hurt against the other.
move: A good impression is specific; ask which quality it is vouching for.
source: Zebrowitz & McDonald, Law and Human Behavior, 1991
reference: Zebrowitz & McDonald, The impact of litigants' baby-facedness and attractiveness on adjudications in small claims courts, Law and Human Behavior, 1991
